text:
Ana Rivera: Quick sync — thinking about a small follow-up to the pipeline RFC: can we gate a tiny "slim-headers" bridge at the edge that strips high-cardinality attrs but preserves a billing_key and provenance? lowers ingest cost but still lets billing reconcile downstream.
CJ Park: short answer: yes, but need to be explicit about which keys are canonical and which we drop.
Michael Li: +1 to the idea. two major tradeoffs: 1) runtime correctness of late-joins, 2) debuggability when we lose attrs at the source.
Ana Rivera: Exactly. proposal sketch: at edge, produce envelope {billing_key, tenant_id, provenance, compact_flags, minimal_span_meta} and full attrs kept in a sidecar POST to retention tier (48h) for backfill/recon.
Sara Gupta: Sounds reasonable. how does this affect sampling and attribution? if sample happens after the bridge we might lose attribution for unsampled flows.
CJ Park: we must make sampling decision at edge if we plan to drop attrs. Otherwise we need a lightweight pointer (trace_id + sidecar ref) so late samples can fetch full attrs during enrichment.
Ana Rivera: pointer idea is good. minimal overhead: add header x-attr-ref: sha256(trace_id+ts) and keep mapping in short-lived store (48h).
Michael Li: Implementation notes: cache key explosion is a risk. limit by TTL + LRU and only create refs for traces with billing-sensitive ops (predicate on route/model).
Sara Gupta: What about cost accounting for multi-model routing? billing_key must be stable and derivable from minimal meta. We should avoid opaque pointers for billing.
CJ Park: Agreed. billing_key derivation rule: prefer tenant_billing_id if present else fallback to hashed(tenant_id + route). That rule must be computed at edge before pruning.
Ana Rivera: Pseudocode we can copy into the edge agent:
```
if has(tenant_billing_id): billing_key = tenant_billing_id
else: billing_key = sha256(tenant_id + '|' + route)
if sensitive_attrs.present and route in billing_sensitive_routes:
  attr_ref = sha256(trace_id + now())
  store_shortlived(attr_ref, full_attrs, ttl=48h)
  emit_envelope(billing_key, attr_ref, minimal_meta)
else:
  emit_envelope(billing_key, null, minimal_meta)
```
CJ Park: Nice. ops concerns: storing full_attrs for 48h needs encryption and RBAC — default to KMS-wrapped at rest and only accessible to enrichment workers.
Sara Gupta: Also need a fallback when sidecar store is unavailable: either emit envelope with full_attrs (higher cost) or mark trace as "degraded-attr" and route to safe fallback model.
Michael Li: Can we piggyback this on existing short-lived cache (existing enrichment-cache service) rather than stand up new one? reuse reduces ops burden.
Ana Rivera: Good call. reuse enrichment-cache. CJ can you model expected storage volume? rough calc: 1KB avg attrs * 1M traces/day * 10% flagged => ~100GB/day retention -> with 48h = 200GB hot. costs ~ affordable but need CIAM review.
CJ Park: I'll run numbers and drop a small spreadsheet in the thread later. initial thought: we should also add per-route enablement toggle in rollout config so we can A/B and abort quickly.
Sara Gupta: Rollout plan: canary 1% of prod traffic on non-critical routes for 24h, monitor billing delta + queryability + SLI for "attr-missing" 404s.
ingest-bot: Note: created deploy checklist item #3124 for "edge-slim-headers-gate" (assignee: CJ Park). :robot_face:
Ana Rivera: Action items: CJ -> capacity numbers + config toggle PR; Michael -> enrichment-cache reuse feasibility; Sara -> SLO checks and canary plan; me -> small RFC update with pseudocode. target: land feature flag and tests in 2 sprints.
CJ Park: ack. I'll post the spreadsheet and a short perf estimate by EOD tomorrow.
Michael Li: I'll spike on cache integration tomorrow and post notes.
Sara Gupta: I'll draft canary SLOs and add them to the checklist.
Ana Rivera: Thanks everyone. If we hit a surprising edge-case we fallback to emitting full_attrs (safest) until fixed. :thumbsup:
